_doc: Example soak/SLO config for the RealWorld 'Conduit' SUT (P4 DB_POOL_SIZE fault). A task COPIES this file and tunes the numbers from oracle runs. Keys starting with '_' are ignored (they are docs). The verifier drives THIS load; nothing here is read from the app's own counters.
_target: Overridden by --target / SOAK_TARGET at runtime; the dokku app container name:port (direct container-name path, NOT the nginx vhost).
_health: If health never returns <500 within health_timeout_s -> infra_error result (reward 0, tagged infra_error), NOT a silent pass.
_load: warmup is discarded (absorbs the agent's redeploy blips). soak is the measured window. rps is the offered rate; workers must exceed peak in-flight (>= rps * request_timeout_s). CALIBRATE rps from an oracle run so the FIXED (large-pool) app clears the gates and the BROKEN (DB_POOL_SIZE=1) app fails them.
_gates: Pass iff (per-driver AND overall) goodput_ratio >= goodput_min AND error_rate <= error_rate_max. goodput = correct/offered (semantic: marker read back / 2xx). error_rate = failures/offered (transport error or HTTP>=500, e.g. the 503 pool-timeout). CALIBRATE against oracle: fixed app should sit well above goodput_min; broken app should breach error_rate_max under the pool-timeout 503s.

bootstrap._doc: Optional: register+login once before the soak to obtain a token. The token is injected wherever a header value contains {token}. Remove this block if the SUT needs no auth for the driven flows.

flows.name: write_readback
flows._doc: POST an article whose title embeds a unique {marker}; extract the returned slug; GET it back and assert the marker text is present. This is the DB-write path that serializes when DB_POOL_SIZE=1.

flows.name: read_feed
flows._doc: GET the global feed. Also DB-bound, but read-only; contrasts with the write path.

findings._doc: Grades /workspace/findings.json. The agent CANNOT see this spec. required_keys must be present and non-empty. Every regex in mechanism_regexes must match (case-insensitive) somewhere in the joined string values. For the P4 fault, force the agent to name the connection pool as the mechanism (must mention 'pool' AND 'connection'/'conn'). Add e.g. 'DB_POOL_SIZE' as a required substring if you want the exact knob named.
